description:
FILED s517 (Fable, 2026-10-15 23:0x) while watching the fresh board base run (`base-result.sh main23`, log ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/base-main23.log).

MEASURED: every board file runs as
    sbcl --control-stack-size 512 --noinform --non-interactive --load <root>/cl/pcl-runtime.lisp --eval "(setf pcl::*pcl-skip-cache* t)" --load /tmp/run-dist-t_PID.lisp
(tools/run-dist-t.pl line ~92, a hand-written command line) -- SOURCE MODE: no `--core`, the runtime loaded and compiled from source for each of the 356 files.  The base log is 171,000 lines of SBCL compiler notes after 17 minutes (`; in: defun %pcl-super-fallback`, the `%p-announce-ef-fallback` style-warning, repeated per file).  At ~25 s of runtime compile per file over 4 jobs that is ~37 minutes -- the board's measured 2,023 s wall (s516b) is almost entirely runtime compile, and so is every agent's board leg and every merge's base result (one slot, ~33 min each, three agents per round).

THE RULE IT BREAKS (CLAUDE.md Quick Reference, task #344): the runners that spawn SBCL share ONE command-line builder, tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm (`sbcl_prefix` / `sbcl_prefix_str`: --core placement, $STACK_MB, the saved-core resolution order) -- "a runner chooses WHAT to load, never HOW SBCL starts; one drifting runner is how #324 measured PCL on a 2 MB stack for months".  run-dist-t.pl is the sixth runner and it drifted when it became the board's engine (s516b #3241; it predates the saved core, s439).  tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl:198 shows the shape: `PCLSbcl::sbcl_prefix_str(runtime => $runtime, quote => 0)` + the caller's own --eval / --load.

FIX (a runner change; the WHAT-TO-RUN table's runners row): build the prefix with `PCLSbcl::sbcl_prefix_str(runtime => "$root/cl/pcl-runtime.lisp", quote => 0)` (core mode when the cached core exists -- it is built on first use and keyed by the runtime's absolute path, so a worktree gets its own), keep the `--eval "(setf pcl::*pcl-skip-cache* t)"` and `--load $lisp`; `PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1` must print the command; `PCL_NO_CORE=1` must give today's source-mode line.  Also read why `*pcl-skip-cache*` is set (the module fasl cache for dist tests) and say whether the core changes anything about it (it should not: the core holds the runtime, the module cache holds transpiled modules).

BAR: the board on ONE tree with the old and the new runner, verdicts and rows IDENTICAL file by file (`tools/cpan-scoreboard.pl --diff` + the per-file LOST check) -- the fresh base `~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/base/dc87c403/` (taken s517 with the old runner on wt-main23 = cd8c276c) is the old half; the new half runs on the same worktree; wall time before / after quoted (`uptime` beside it); `tools/t/` has no row for run-dist-t -- add one that checks the spawned line comes from PCLSbcl (the shape of tools/t/sbcl-prefix.t), and a Pl/t row if the gate has a runner-drift guard to extend (grep Pl/t for sbcl_prefix).  A verdict that MOVES is a finding (a file that passed only because source mode differs from the core -- e.g. a load-order or a `*features*` difference) and is read, not blessed.


=== DONE (s517a, commit ee622fb8, 2026-10-15) ===
tools/run-dist-t.pl now builds its line with PCLSbcl::sbcl_prefix_str(runtime =>
"$root/cl/pcl-runtime.lisp", quote => 0) + its own `--eval "(setf
pcl::*pcl-skip-cache* t)" --load $lisp`; PCL_SHOW_SBCL=1 prints
`SBCL[run-dist-t]: ...`; PCL_NO_CORE=1 gives the old source-mode line byte for
byte (a tools/t row asserts it).  *pcl-skip-cache* governs the MODULE fasl cache
(dist test modules transpile fresh), not the runtime: the core changes nothing
there.
A/B on the s517a tree (member 0 committed), ONE dist, Text-Balanced-2.07-0,
--jobs 2: --tsv and --rows IDENTICAL (54 lines; only the `# Command:` header
differs); wall 89 s (old) -> 41 s (new), load average 5.8-6.6 (uptime in
scratch/s517a/ab2959.log).  Guard: tools/t/run-dist-t-sbcl.t (6 rows).  The
whole-board old-vs-new is Fable's (base/dc87c403 taken with the old runner).
subject: tools/run-dist-t.pl (the CPAN board's per-file runner) spawns SBCL by hand in SOURCE MODE -- every board file recompiles the 25k-line runtime (~25 s), the whole 33-minute board is ~90 % runtime compile; route it through PCLSbcl (the ONE builder, task #344) and the saved core
